topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and an overview of the lecture themes.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental concepts of how the innate immune system detects infections and damage using PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and signaling mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific receptor systems that detect danger signals, including toll-like receptors, cytosolic PRR families, and inflammasome complexes.

topics.label: Inflammatory response execution, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow the progression of the acute inflammatory response from sentinel cell triggering and leukocyte extravasation to lymphatic priming and systemic inflammatory complications.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms that terminate inflammation, regenerate injured tissue, and establish chronic containment structures when pathogens persist.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the conclusion of the lecture and previews the next topic.
